solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where to start digging gold in a lode possibly?

definitions.text: Where to start digging gold in a lode possibly?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters gathered from the clue may be rearranged
the start of the word digging supplies its opening letter

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A prospector wonders where to begin digging for gold in a likely vein of ore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges D (the start of 'digging'), OR and A LODE together. The whole clue doubles as the definition: the fabled city of gold is where you would dig.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought in South America is exactly the place a gold-digger would start.

clue.text: Art supporters, sly types after women's lib?

indicators.note: lib, short for liberation, means the W is freed from the word and so dropped

parts.note: weasels are sly, cunning people
W is the standard abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: Artistic backers of feminism are dismissed as sly operators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after women's lib' plays on Women's Lib, the 1970s liberation movement: the W is liberated, i.e. removed, from WEASELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters' stands hold up canvases, so they literally support art.

clue.text: Eg Baron Cohen lookalike dashed across the pond

parts.note: a double is someone who looks just like another
in American English to barrel along is to rush at speed, so dashed

explanation.surface: Someone resembling the comedian Sacha Baron Cohen rushed over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' means in America: barrel as a verb for speeding is US slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname of two linked parts, like Baron Cohen, is called a double-barrelled name.

clue.text: Like some of the wind cure Mike ignored

indicators.note: ignored says the M is left out of the word for cure

parts.note: a remedy is a cure
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A treatment for flatulence fails because someone named Mike was overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wind' is not weather or flatulence but the wind section of an orchestra, where oboes and clarinets sound reedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind instruments with reeds give a thin, piping tone described as reedy.

clue.text: GP was rude about leading lady's bloomers

indicators.note: about says the letters for the doctor and the jumbled word go around the lady

parts.note: a GP, a general practitioner, is a doctor, abbreviated DR

indicators.note: rude, in the sense of rough or crude, signals the word was is roughly rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the nation's leading lady

explanation.surface: A family doctor was insulting about the actress's mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' turns WAS into AWS, giving DRAWS, which goes 'about' ER to make the answer. Bloomers are not blunders here but old-fashioned underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are names for long, loose knickers once worn by women.

clue.text: 19 goods, sweet

parts.note: the answer to 19 is the French city Nice, so goods as said there are bon and bon, French for good
the answer to 19 is the French city Nice, so goods as said there are bon and bon, French for good

explanation.surface: Merchandise from the Riviera is charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is NICE, read as the French city: its 'goods' are two French words for good, BON BON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonbon is a small sugary confection, a type of candy.

clue.text: A lot can go wrong with quite a few sides

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of the phrase are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Many things can go awry when you have lots of partners on your side.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eight sides, which is quite a few for a flat shape.

clue.text: This showed bottle in RAF, a bit shattered

definitions.text: This showed bottle in RAF, a bit shattered

indicators.note: shattered signals the letters of those words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: This campaign proved the courage of the air force pilots, who were rather exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage. The whole clue is the definition: the 1940 air campaign proved the RAF's nerve, its pilots worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1940 air battle over southern England, won by the Royal Air Force, is famed for its pilots' courage.

clue.text: Nobody grasps second missile's point

indicators.note: grasps says the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: nobody means no one

explanation.surface: Nobody understands the purpose of a second rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is the tip of a rocket rather than its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed front section of a rocket or missile is its cone-shaped tip.

clue.text: In which to cook odd bits of 10 pecan nuts

indicators.note: odd bits of picks the first, third and fifth letters of that word

parts.note: the answer to 10, a word for standing

indicators.note: nuts, meaning crazy, signals the letters of pecan are scrambled

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for odd pieces of ten crazy pecan nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' takes S, A, U from STATUS (the answer to 10); 'nuts' rearranges PECAN to CEPAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep metal pan with a handle is the vessel for boiling and stewing on a hob.

clue.text: Standing stone figures earl discarded

indicators.note: discarded says the E is thrown away from the word for figures

parts.note: statues are carved stone figures

explanation.surface: Upright stone statues of an earl have been thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's standing is their position or rank in society.

clue.text: Where guys are tense and theatrical

definitions.meaning: guys are tent ropes, pulled taut where tents are pitched
exaggerated, affected and over the top

explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' are not men but tent ropes, kept tight at a site of tents.
explanation.definitionFit: A site of tents and an affected, showy manner are both senses of this word.

clue.text: Without notice, lady invests old students' dough

indicators.note: invests means the remaining letters clothe, or surround, the other pieces
without says the notice is removed from the word lady

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
L is a learner driver, so two students give LL

explanation.surface: A lady secretly puts money into some former students' bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing AD from LADY leaves LY, which 'invests' O and LL. 'dough' is money, not bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for money or cash.

clue.text: Old Protestant Welshman set in charge

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh first name
to gel is to set firm

explanation.surface: A Welshman in his evangelical church is set in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for an evangelical, a Protestant stressing the gospel.

clue.text: Manhattan products flop when bottled

indicators.note: bottled says one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a bomb is a flop, a failure

explanation.surface: Manhattan cocktails fail when served bottled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manhattan' is not the cocktail but the Manhattan Project, which produced the first atomic bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime Manhattan Project built the first atomic weapons.

clue.text: Maoist nut translated Origin of Species

indicators.note: translated signals that the letters are converted into another form

explanation.surface: A Maoist zealot has translated Darwin's famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Origin of Species' is not Darwin's title here but literally what gives rise to new species.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic changes are the source from which new species evolve.

clue.text: It spans river junction in 12

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for twelve

parts.note: twelve o'clock midday is noon
a T-junction gives T

explanation.surface: A bridge crosses the river at a junction at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 here is the number, the hour of noon, not a cross-reference to the answer at 12.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating bridge built on boats spans a river.

clue.text: Drizzle almost bound to upset horny beast

indicators.note: almost drops the final letter of the word

parts.note: to bound is to spring

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: an elk is an antlered animal

explanation.surface: Light rain is about to unsettle a horned creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SPRING to SPRIN; 'upset' turns ELK to KLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter small drops of liquid is to drizzle them, as over a salad.

clue.text: Upright piano tuner worked without one

indicators.note: worked signals that the letters are reshaped, here once the letters of one are taken out

explanation.surface: An honest piano tuner works without any help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one': remove O, N, E from PIANO TUNER, then 'worked' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A morally strict person is upright, and the word also describes such strictness.

clue.text: Northern Rock's described as friendly

parts.note: rock and ice are both slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: The bank Northern Rock is described as amiable.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Rock was a British bank that famously failed in 2007; here it is just N plus a slang word for a diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and friendly are both words for pleasant and kind.

clue.text: Big names export drug from Sulawesi

indicators.note: export means send out, so the E leaves the old name

parts.note: Celebes is the former name of the Indonesian island
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Famous people trade narcotics out of an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities are famous people, well-known stars.

clue.text: Where to train sheepdog, say, for one

indicators.note: for says the example takes the place of one

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog breed
I is the Roman numeral one
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A place for teaching a sheepdog, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' stands for EG, and 'for one' swaps it into COLLIE for the I.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is a place of higher education and training.

clue.text: Penny is the French version — I'm used to pound

parts.note: in French is is est and the is le
in French is is est and the is le

explanation.surface: The penny is the French equivalent to the pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is not currency, despite 'Penny', but to crush, as in a mortar.
explanation.definitionFit: A club-shaped tool for crushing things in a mortar.

clue.text: I make an impression with one brief visit in uniform

parts.note: to dent is to make an impression in a surface
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: brief means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a call is a visit

explanation.surface: Someone makes an impression with one short visit while in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly alike, all the same, as things in uniform are.

clue.text: A Lloyd Webber's partner's moment?

parts.note: Andrew (A) Lloyd Webber's lyricist partner is T(im) Rice
Andrew (A) Lloyd Webber's lyricist partner is T(im) Rice

explanation.surface: A composer's partner has a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Lloyd Webber wrote musicals with lyricist Tim Rice; with initials, A Lloyd Webber's partner is T Rice.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trice means in a moment, very quickly.

clue.text: Tiny dry biting comment

indicators.note: biting says the outer pieces close their teeth around the inner

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A tiny teetotaller makes a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A short online post on Twitter is a brief comment.

clue.text: He was here backing royal house over Israel

indicators.note: over places the code across the reversed house, with it inside
backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: York was an English royal house
IL is Israel's international code

explanation.surface: Someone supporting the royal house of York interfered with Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He was here' is the Second World War graffiti: Kilroy was here.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous wartime graffiti, Kilroy was here, names the man who was there.

clue.text: Material on Near East?

parts.note: re means on or concerning
the Levant is the Near East, the eastern Mediterranean

explanation.surface: Fabric about the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: Material, as in material evidence, means pertinent to the matter.

clue.text: This son held estate implicitly

indicators.note: implicitly says the answer is contained in the words, not stated outright

explanation.surface: This son was held to inherit the estate by implication.
explanation.walkthrough: The firstborn son traditionally inherits the estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn of several sons is the oldest one.

clue.text: Feeling disheartened in life perhaps

indicators.note: disheartened removes the heart, the middle letter, of the word

parts.note: sentience is the capacity for feeling

explanation.surface: Feeling downcast in one's life, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life' is a prison term, a life sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A life term is a prison sentence, so life is an example.
